summary: Source-anchored research for Trailing participial analysis phrases. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Watch-list participles named by the Wikipedia guide: highlighting/underscoring/emphasizing, reflecting/symbolizing, contributing to, cultivating/fostering, enhancing. It treats the tell as stronger when the verb's subject is an inanimate fact or event. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)

Reinhart et al. (CMU/NJIT, arXiv 2410.16107, Oct 2024) found instruction-tuned models use present participial clauses at 2-5x the human rate: GPT-4o 527%, GPT-4o Mini 481%, Llama 3 70B Instruct 261%, 8B Instruct 224%, versus base models near human levels (94-102%). (low confidence)

Wikipedia's Signs of AI writing guide says chatbots attach a present-participle (-ing) phrase at sentence end to add superficial analysis of significance, recognition or impact, sometimes with vague attributions; on Wikipedia such comments are usually synthesis or unattributed opinion. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)
Base Llama 3 models show human-like participial rates, so the excess is introduced by instruction tuning, not pretraining. (low confidence)

The pattern is only a potential sign, not proof: the Wikipedia guide says such patterns also occur in human writing (editorials, fan fiction) and human style is increasingly influenced by LLMs. (medium confidence)

Stylometric detectors relying on surface features show high false positives and poor domain transfer (Pudasaini et al., arXiv 2603.23146), so a participial-phrase count alone should not be used to accuse text of being AI-written. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)
